new_statements.quote: 2.5 Tone change. A conspicuous tone change can be observed within ch'ü tone syllables in composite words; they are pronounced with a high level tone, though the same words in isolation are pronounced with a low falling tone. ʔiɛn21 'seal' : ʔiɛn55-tuat5 'printing'. This change takes place only in syllables not occurring as final in a phonemic phrase. The final syllables of phonemic phrases never undergo the change described when those syllables carry the primary or the secondary stress: kan55-ʔbu53 'a cadre' but siu24-kan21 'a tree trunk'; ki55-miɛn24 'to meet' but mɔ24-ki21 'to see'.

new_statements.rule_in_words: Wen-ch'ang Hainanese is a seven-tone language (yin-p'ing 24, yang-p'ing 33, shang 53 staccato, ch'ü 21, yin-ju 5, yang-ju 3). The only remark on stress is embedded in the tone-sandhi rule: the final syllable of a 'phonemic phrase' (tone group / compound) bears primary or secondary stress and keeps its citation tone, while non-final syllables are the sandhi (weak) positions (ch'ü 21 > 55). I.e. prominence is described as phrase-/compound-final, Southern-Min style; no independent word-stress rule is given. Hashimoto 1959 additionally transcribes toneless 'light-tone' (軽声, marked 0) particles, i.e. unstressed enclitic syllables exist.
new_statements.secondary_stress: Mentions 'the primary or the secondary stress' on phrase-final syllables without defining where secondary stress falls.
new_statements.exceptions: Sandhi (and hence the stress remark) applies only to non-final ch'ü-tone syllables in composite words; Ting-an dialect 'has no tone sandhi' (p. 10/frame 16) and nothing is said about its stress. Sentence-final particles are written with neutral tone 0 in Hashimoto 1959.
new_statements.domain_note: Domain is the 'phonemic phrase' (compound word / tone group), not the morpheme-syllable; statement concerns citation vs. combination forms of disyllabic compounds.
new_statements.identity_note: The quoted statement describes the Wen-ch'ang (Wenchang 文昌, 'Bon-shio/Bun-sio') dialect, the prestige variety of Hainanese (Glottolog lists Wenchang as a dialect under hain1238). The same 1971 guide's Ting-an (定安) section (analysis by J. Norman) says only 'Ting-an has no tone sandhi' and nothing on stress. Nakajima 2002 describes the Wanning (万寧) dialect and is silent on stress.

sources.note: Ch. 2 (pp. 5-8, frames 10-14) gives syllable structure, initials, finals, 7 tones, and sec. 2.5 'Tone change': ch'u-tone (21) syllables become high level (55) when non-final in a phonemic phrase; 'The final syllables of phonemic phrases never undergo the change described when those syllables carry the primary or the secondary stress' (p. 7). No separate stress section; Ting-an part: 'Ting-an has no tone sandhi', nothing on stress. Only occurrence of 'stress' in the whole text layer.

sources.citation: Hashimoto, Mantaro. 1960. The Bon-shio (文昌) dialect of Hainan: a historical and comparative study of its phonological structure. First part: the initials. Gengo Kenkyu 38: 106-135. doi:10.11435/gengo1939.1960.38_106
sources.note: Historical-comparative study of initials; lists 7 tonemes by number only and refers phonetics to an unpublished 'Hainan Phonemics'. Nothing on word stress (one mention of 'unstressed' concerns Pekingese, not Hainanese).

sources.citation: Hashimoto, Mantaro. 1960. The phonemic structure of the Bon-shio dialect of Hainan (Chinese). Conference abstract in 第42回大会発表報告要旨, Gengo Kenkyu 38: 154-157. doi:10.11435/gengo1939.1960.38_148
sources.note: Segmental phonemes and 7 tonemes; 'pitch and stress' curves of isolated tones measured with a Pitch-Stress Recorder (intensity of citation tones, not word-stress placement); notes the high-level sandhi tone of yin-ch'u. No statement of stress position.

sources.citation: 橋本萬太郎 (Hashimoto Mantaro). 1959. 海南語音韻論―「文昌」方言の音声論と音韻法則 (分科会報告). 中国語学 91: 12-16. doi:10.7131/chuugokugogaku.1959.91_12
sources.note: Japanese conference report on Wenchang phonetics (implosives, sound laws) with sample texts; states tones are written with Arabic numerals and '特にOにより軽声を表す' (0 marks the light/neutral tone), i.e. toneless unstressed particles (ma0, la0, nji0) are transcribed. No rule for stress placement.
